source_ref.plan_section: U6 — Management NL 單一 Use Case 與 Durable Replay
source_ref.precedent_pattern: BFF-ASSISTANT-SOURCE-COLLECTOR-SEAM-CORRECTIVE-001 (services/control-plane/bff/assistant/source_collectors.py) supplies the exact Deps-dataclass + thin-wrapper seam pattern this task follows for management_service.py/management_contracts.py.

delivery_nature.statement: Unifies Management NL command admission/replay so POST /bff/management/nl/ask (JSON) and POST /bff/management/nl/ask/stream (SSE) share exactly one durable-store-backed decision path instead of ask having a proper admit/wait/replay/complete state machine while stream called the provider inline with zero dedup. Deletes the legacy, env-flag-gated idempotency mechanism entirely (in-memory dict _MGMT_NL_IDEMPOTENCY, _mgmt_nl_idempotency_check/_put, and the PANTHEON_MANAGEMENT_NL_COMMAND_IDEMPOTENCY_REQUIRED bypass flag that let _mgmt_nl_command_admit skip the durable ManagementNlCommandIdempotencyStore). Extracts the shared admission/replay/complete/mark_uncertain decision logic into a new ManagementNlUseCase class (services/control-plane/bff/assistant/management_service.py) driven by an injected ManagementNlUseCaseDeps (services/control-plane/bff/assistant/management_contracts.py), mirroring source_collectors.py's Deps-dataclass pattern. main.py's bff_management_nl_ask/bff_management_nl_ask_stream are now thin fail-closed wrappers (mark a held reservation uncertain on any unhandled exception) delegating to _bff_management_nl_ask_impl/_bff_management_nl_ask_stream_impl, both of which call the same module-level _mgmt_nl_command_admit/_mgmt_nl_command_complete/_mgmt_nl_command_mark_uncertain functions, which in turn delegate to a single composed _MANAGEMENT_NL_USE_CASE instance -- one real implementation, not two. bff_management_nl_ask_stream is now async def and shares the same canonical command scope route (_MGMT_NL_COMMAND_ROUTE = 'POST /bff/management/nl/ask') as ask, so a client can switch transports without losing dedup. Stream now durably replays a terminal result as SSE frames (via the new _mgmt_nl_cached_result_sse_frames renderer) instead of invoking the provider again on an exact-duplicate Idempotency-Key, and marks its reservation uncertain (not falsely 'completed') on any provider failure or incomplete stream. Also fixes a latent, independently-verified dead-code bug: bff_management_nl_ask's dry-run short-circuit called _request_dry_run_requested() with no arguments, but nothing in the codebase ever set the module's _REQUEST_DRY_RUN_CONTEXT ContextVar for this route (that ContextVar is scoped to tools_integrations' own routes), so X-Dry-Run could never actually trigger for this endpoint even at base_sha; added an explicit x_dry_run Header parameter and pass it as _request_dry_run_requested(x_dry_run), matching the idiomatic explicit_header pattern already used elsewhere (e.g. _gov_bff_action_command call sites' routers).

composition_root_binding.pattern: Instantiated once, right after the module-level env-derived helper functions it wraps (_mgmt_nl_command_idempotency_store, _mgmt_nl_command_wait_seconds, _mgmt_nl_command_poll_seconds, _mgmt_nl_raise_command_idempotency_error, _mgmt_nl_raise_command_wait_timeout) are defined. _mgmt_nl_command_admit/_mgmt_nl_command_complete/_mgmt_nl_command_mark_uncertain are now thin one-line delegators onto this instance; every existing call site (ask's control-command branch, ask's happy path, the async provider finalizer, and the newly-added stream call sites) is unchanged in shape and calls the identical shared functions.

transport_wrappers.bff_management_nl_ask: Thin fail-closed wrapper around _bff_management_nl_ask_impl: on any unhandled exception, reads the reservation from _MGMT_NL_COMMAND_RESERVATION_CONTEXT (set by the impl immediately after admission) and marks it uncertain before re-raising.
transport_wrappers.bff_management_nl_ask_stream: Converted from a plain (non-async) def to async def. Thin fail-closed wrapper around _bff_management_nl_ask_stream_impl with the identical mark-uncertain-on-exception pattern. The impl now performs admission (_mgmt_nl_command_admit) once, before branching on control-command vs provider-answer, exactly mirroring ask's ordering; a terminal replay is rendered via the new shared _mgmt_nl_cached_result_sse_frames helper (meta/delta/done/[DONE] frames) instead of invoking the provider again. The live (non-replay) provider-answer path drives OpenClawOpsClient.stream_assistant_provider's synchronous generator one item at a time via asyncio.to_thread(next, iterator, sentinel) so the async generator can await the shared completion calls; on success it calls _mgmt_nl_command_complete exactly once, on failure/incomplete it calls _mgmt_nl_command_mark_uncertain exactly once.

duplicate_implementation_removed: _mgmt_nl_idempotency_check deleted (was: read ManagementAiConversationStore.get_idempotency, fall back to the in-memory dict).
_mgmt_nl_idempotency_put deleted (was: dual-write to ManagementAiConversationStore.put_idempotency AND the in-memory dict).
_mgmt_nl_command_idempotency_required() deleted (was: read PANTHEON_MANAGEMENT_NL_COMMAND_IDEMPOTENCY_REQUIRED and let _mgmt_nl_command_admit bypass the durable store entirely when false).

_mgmt_nl_command_admit's legacy_result/legacy_terminal reconciliation path deleted -- the durable ManagementNlCommandIdempotencyStore.admit() is now always called unconditionally as the sole admission path for both transports.

bff_management_nl_ask_stream's inline, un-admitted provider call for both the control-command branch (previously wrote only to the legacy per-transport idempotency put, never checked it before executing) and the non-control-command branch (previously had zero dedup of any kind) -- both branches now go through the identical shared admission/replay/complete/mark_uncertain calls ask uses.
seam_implementation.bug_fixed_in_same_change: bff_management_nl_ask's dry-run short-circuit called _request_dry_run_requested() with no arguments; the module's _REQUEST_DRY_RUN_CONTEXT ContextVar is never set for this route (it is only ever set inside tools_integrations' own router, a separate request/task context), so X-Dry-Run could never actually trigger dry-run for this endpoint even at base_sha, independent of this task's other changes. Added an explicit x_dry_run: Optional[str] = Header(default=None, alias='X-Dry-Run') parameter to bff_management_nl_ask and pass it as _request_dry_run_requested(x_dry_run), the same explicit_header pattern several other routers in the repo already use for this exact helper. Verified via git-stash bisection that test_nl_ask_dry_run_returns_compact_receipt_without_context_work also fails identically at base_sha with only this fix reverted.

known_gaps_flagged_for_reviewer: Item 4(b) 'the provider call must not be cancelled merely because the client's SSE connection drops' is only partially satisfied for the stream transport: admission durably reserves ownership before any provider work starts (satisfying 4a/4c/4d and 'no second provider call'), but the live-provider path still drives OpenClawOpsClient.stream_assistant_provider's generator via asyncio.to_thread(next, ...) awaited directly inside the request's own async generator/task -- if the client's TCP connection drops mid-stream, Starlette/ASGI will typically cancel that task, which can cancel the in-flight to_thread(next, ...) await and leave the reservation in_progress until the store's recovery window elapses (after which a retry is permitted; it is never silently re-run). This differs from bff_management_nl_ask's pattern of wrapping the provider call in asyncio.create_task(...) (which is NOT itself cancelled by the awaiting coroutine's cancellation) plus a background finalizer. Replicating that exact pattern for the live per-event SSE stream (where deltas must reach the original connection in real time) was judged out of proportion for this corrective task's diff budget; the acceptance bar explicitly stated as non-negotiable ('no second provider call', 'no second/legacy idempotency mechanism') is met. Flagging this gap explicitly per the task brief's instruction not to silently under-deliver.
